newsitem.title: JAPAN: SOCCER-KAWASAKI, HIROSHIMA REACH EMPEROR CUP FINAL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-KAWASAKI, HIROSHIMA REACH EMPEROR CUP FINAL.

text.p: Verdy Kawasaki booked a place in Wednesday's Emperor Cup final against Sanfrecce Hiroshima with a 3-0 semifinal win over Urawa Red Diamonds on Sunday.
Hiroshima reached the final for the second successive year, beating Gamba Osaka 2-0. Neither finalist has won the Cup before.
Verdy, twice J-League champions, were contained until the 57th minute when a 20-metre drive by Brazilian playmaker Bismarck was deflected off team mate Kazuyoshi Miura and rolled into the net.
Yasutoshi Miura, Kazuyoshi's elder brother, added the second in the 70th minute and Kurihara put the result beyond doubt with a goal seven minutes from time.
It was a disappointing farewell for Urawa's manager Holger Osieck and fellow German midfielder Uwe Bein, who are both leaving the club.
In the other semifinal at Nagai stadium in Osaka, first-half goals by South Korean forward Noh Jung Yoon and Brazilian midfielder Santos saw Hiroshima through.
They needed some good fortune, however, as Gamba had two second-half goals disallowed while Dutch striker Hans Gillhaus was twice denied by the woodwork.
